criteria.criterion: Grep of .github/workflows/ci.yml: every athena-bin cache key (all restore and save steps) uses hashFiles covering crates/**, xtask/**, rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, athena.toml, defaults.toml, setup.sh and docs/system-facts.md. In each of the fmt, clippy and test jobs, actions/cache/restore steps for gitleaks and the athena binary come before the step named 'Set up (pinned toolchain, gitleaks, athena)'.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. All 9 athena-bin key lines (6 restore steps, 3 save steps) use hashFiles('crates/**', 'xtask/**', 'rust-toolchain.toml', 'Cargo.toml', 'Cargo.lock', 'athena.toml', 'defaults.toml', 'setup.sh', 'docs/system-facts.md'). The restore steps sit after the target-cache restore and before setup. athena_bin_keys_cover_every_compiled_in_file and every_job_restores_the_tool_caches_before_it_runs_the_setup_step both passed on the real ci.yml.

criteria.criterion: ci.yml has matching actions/cache/save steps with the existing condition (not a pull request, ref equal to the default branch, no exact cache hit). Every uses: line is pinned by a 40-character SHA. History, attribution and pr-head also restore before setup, or a comment states why they do not. No other workflow behavior changes.
criteria.evidence: Each save step uses actions/cache/save@5a3ec84e… with `github.event_name != 'pull_request' && github.ref == format('refs/heads/{0}', …default_branch) && steps.cache-*.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'`. The test job adds `matrix.shard == 0`. history, attribution and pr-head restore before setup, and a comment says they restore only. The diff only adds steps and header comments; no other steps changed. every_action_is_pinned_by_a_full_commit_sha passed. The ci_shards tests (20) and the existing pass-marker policy test passed under `cargo test -p xtask`.

criteria.criterion: xtask has one shared list of athena build inputs that both the skip digest and the policy test read. The comment in ci.yml and the CHANGELOG do not claim more than the key covers.
criteria.evidence: BUILD_INPUT_GLOBS is a const [&str; 9] in xtask/src/main.rs. input_files/inputs_digest iterate it, and build_inputs_command prints it. The command printed exactly the nine globs. policy.rs gets the list from that subcommand (build_input_globs) and requires set equality with every key. The ci.yml comment and the CHANGELOG name exactly the nine globs and say CHANGELOG.md, README.md and the rest of docs/ are not in the key.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p xtask`. A test edits one compiled-in file (a prompt .md under a temp copy of the tree) and asserts the inputs digest changes. Another asserts the skip happens with a matching digest and cached binary and does not happen with a mismatched digest or no binary, and a third asserts the stamp is not left stale after a non-CI build.
criteria.evidence: All 52 unit tests passed, including tests::the_inputs_digest_changes_when_a_compiled_in_file_is_edited, tests::skip_only_with_ci_matching_stamp_and_binary and tests::a_non_ci_build_leaves_no_stale_stamp. Their bodies: the first edits crates/athena-context/prompts/producer.md in a temp tree, then docs/system-facts.md, then a new file under crates/, then each exact file, and asserts the digest changes each time; a CHANGELOG.md edit does not change it. The second covers ci true/false, a missing binary, a missing stamp and a mismatched digest. The third checks that the stamp is gone while the build closure runs, holds D2 afterwards, and is absent after a failed build.

The new tests derive the compiled-in file set from include_str!/include_bytes! targets and the manifests, and fail if any athena-bin hashFiles key in ci.yml misses one. They also fail on a ci.yml variant with a restore step removed or placed after the setup step.

findings.summary: The CHANGELOG says the key 'reads' the shared list. In fact the ci.yml key is a hard-coded copy that a test keeps equal to it.
findings.evidence: ci.yml spells out the nine globs literally in nine places. Only policy.rs check_athena_bin_keys ties them to BUILD_INPUT_GLOBS. The ci.yml header comment phrases this accurately ('hashes exactly the nine globs that … prints'); the CHANGELOG wording is looser.
findings.location: CHANGELOG.md (new entry), 'the key, the build skip's digest and the policy test all read it'

findings.summary: The include scanner treats everything after the first `#[cfg(test)]` in a file as test code, so it is a heuristic.
findings.evidence: `text.split("#[cfg(test)]").next()` would miss a production include_str! placed after an early `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;`. The doc comment states this limit, and the crates/** and xtask/** globs still cover any such target inside those directories. Only a new compiled-in file outside crates/ and xtask/, placed after such a line, would slip through. A more exact alternative is to scope by item (for example with syn). I checked the current tree, and every include target the scan skips is test-only.

findings.summary: input_files follows directory symlinks while walking, so a symlink loop under crates/ or xtask/ would recurse forever.
findings.evidence: `path.is_dir()` follows symlinks. The repository has none there today, so this is only a robustness gap.

summary: The change does what the retry asked for. ci.yml now restores a gitleaks cache and an athena binary cache before 'Set up (pinned toolchain, gitleaks, athena)' in fmt, clippy, test, history, attribution and pr-head. fmt, clippy and test shard 0 save both caches, on the default branch only and not after an exact hit. Every athena-bin key hashes the nine globs: crates/**, xtask/**, rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, athena.toml, defaults.toml, setup.sh and docs/system-facts.md. Those globs are one const, BUILD_INPUT_GLOBS, in xtask/src/main.rs. The `setup --ci` skip digest reads it, and `xtask build-inputs` prints it. A policy test requires every athena-bin key to equal that list and to cover every production include_str!/include_bytes! target plus the manifests. Mutant tests show that a missing glob, a missing restore, or a restore after setup is rejected. Unit tests show three things: editing a prompt or docs/system-facts.md changes the digest; the build is skipped only with --ci, a binary and a matching stamp; and a rebuild removes the stamp first and writes it only after success. I ran `cargo test -p xtask`, `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` and `cargo run -p xtask -- build-inputs`, and all passed or printed the expected nine globs. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full test runs passed. I found only minor issues: the CHANGELOG wording about the shared list is slightly loose, and the include scanner has a heuristic limit that the change itself documents.
